solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

R058-01.notes: Passage moves from the old account (P1) to the 2002 revision (P2) to what it enabled (tearless onion, P3-4). A: passage reports GM onions weren't sold; it never argues they should be. C: garlic is a chemical contrast, not a cooking-preference comparison. D: kitchen tips are only P5, too narrow.

R058-02.notes: P2: 'a second enzyme seizes most of it [the intermediate] first and converts it into a volatile compound that is the real irritant.' A: that is alliinase's job. B: in garlic the intermediate reacts with itself, no enzyme. C: reverses/misstates; flavor compounds are not made from the irritant.

R058-03.notes: 'The trouble was...' garlic has alliinase doing the same work yet no tears, so the old account was incomplete. B: contradicted, alliinase works in garlic. C: passage says same intermediate path, not a different starting material. D: no preference claim.

R058-04.notes: Enzyme grabs/takes hold of the intermediate before it reacts with itself. A: understanding is irrelevant. B: confiscate implies legal authority taking property. D: 'attacks suddenly' is a tempting connotation but the sense is capturing/taking, not attacking.

R058-05.notes: P3: with the enzyme off, 'the intermediate compound might follow the garlic-like path instead,' keeping or gaining flavor; P4 confirms higher other flavor sulfur compounds. A: about chilling, irrelevant to flavor. B: no claim alliinase produces more stored compounds (and it breaks them down, not produces them). C: contradicts the logic; removing irritant would then reduce flavor.

R058-06.notes: Near-verbatim from P4. B: they released 'far less' irritant. C: analysis found higher flavor compounds. D: the bred onion was by a Japanese company sold in Japan, and nothing says it preceded or blocked the GM onions.

R058-07.notes: Sentence says tricks reduce formation/arrival but don't stop the reaction: clarifies scope and limits. A: P5 opens saying the advice 'makes sense' chemically. C: no new method follows; P6 turns to the onion's defense. D: no reference to bred onions there.

R058-08.notes: Sharp knife works by crushing fewer cells, releasing less starting material; fewer, cleaner cuts likewise rupture fewer cells. A: refrigeration = chilling, works by slowing enzymes/evaporation. B: window works by carrying irritant away. D: distance reduces how much arrives, an arrival mechanism like B.

R058-09.notes: P6: the chemistry 'appears to be a defense' against animals biting the bulb; affecting cooks is incidental. A: no breeding for more irritant; breeding went the other way. B: P5 says no trick stops the reaction. C: the 2002 work explains production.

R058-10.notes: P1: cutting ruptures cells, the stored sulfur compounds and alliinase meet, reactions begin; this precedes intermediate formation. B: second enzymatic step. C: after irritant forms. D: garlic path, not the onion irritant path.

R058-11.notes: 'Until the light went thin' = dimming late-afternoon light, i.e., faint. A and C are physical-shape senses of thin; D (sharp) does not fit fading light.

R058-12.notes: 'If I wrote the reason down, it would come out smaller than it was' = reduce something meaningful to an inadequate explanation. A: daughter not involved. B: narrator says 'I thought I knew'; no worry about being wrong. C: narrator chose not to write it, and the concern is diminishment, not proving attention.

R058-13.notes: First-person 'I' who helped plant, lives on the street ('our street', watches from 'my window'), and 'I was fourteen' signals retrospection. A: Halvorsen is 'he' and never explains. B: the mother is observed in third person. D: narrator is first-person and limited ('I kept waiting for him to explain').
